speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Street hawking, or the peddling of goods on the streets, was common in Singapore several decades ago.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If we look at the old photos of street hawking, we can see the poor hygiene conditions, the pollution of waterways, the piles of waste that attracted pests, the potential fire hazards and the obstruction to traffic that resulted in disamenities to the residents at such localities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Government thus undertook to relocate the street hawkers to purpose-built hawker centres and markets.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many street hawkers had made the transition well, making use of the sheltered facilities to sell their goods and going on to expand their offerings.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, not all the street hawkers were resettled and 31 rag-and-bone men were given permits to continue their trade at the Sungei Road site in view of their chosen trade.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In 2000, when their permits expired, the site was designated as the Sungei Road Hawking Zone (SRHZ).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Only 11 of the 31 original permit holders still remain today.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Through the years, many others have taken the opportunity to peddle their goods for free at SRHZ.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, the activities of SRHZ have resulted in disamenities, such as the obstruction of roads and the storage of goods in surrounding areas, including the nearby drains and housing estate, posing risks to public health and incurring additional public resources for the upkeep of the public areas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Despite this, we have continued to allow SRHZ to remain in operation for as long as we could, even though the area has been zoned for residential use.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, when the Jalan Besar Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station was being constructed in 2011, instead of removing the whole SRHZ, the size of SRHZ was reduced as required, so that SRHZ could continue to stay open.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We understand that SRHZ holds memories for some Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The National Heritage Board (NHB), therefore, conducted research and documentation to preserve the memories of the site for future generations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: A virtual tour of the site as well as other resources are available on NHB's heritage portal, "roots.sg".

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Singaporeans have also contributed their personal stories, photographs and videos on social media.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Since 2012, we have informed the Association for the Recycling of Second Hand Goods that notice would be given to the users of SRHZ to cease their operations once the development plans for the Sungei Road area are confirmed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We note that there are calls, including a Petition presented earlier by the Member, Mr Kok Heng Leun, for SRHZ to be relocated.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, SRHZ users who wish to continue their trade can do so at appropriate venues, such as hawker centres, where there are better facilities and necessary amenities for users to conduct their businesses, or at existing flea markets, where these activities can be properly managed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is similar to how street hawkers in the past have moved on to purpose-built hawker centres and markets.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Users may also take advantage of the opportunities that these new business locations present.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, Mdm Tan Guo Mei, who was featured in the news recently, took the opportunity when she moved to a lock-up stall at a hawker centre to expand her offerings to include new goods which she can sell at all times and not be exposed to the weather elements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Other SRHZ users who have taken up such stalls have also indicated that they intend to move on to also sell new items, such as shoes and accessories, beyond the second-hand items that they used to sell.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For all other users, we have offered a 50% rental rebate for the first two years on a goodwill basis, provided they live in public housing and do not own more than one property.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So far, 29 SRHZ users have been allocated a lock-up stall.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many of these stalls are clustered at two popular hawker centres not too far from SRHZ − the Chinatown Market and the Golden Mile Food Centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Hawkers' Associations at these two centres have, in fact, invited the SRHZ users who have taken up stalls there to join them, which is an important step to help the users integrate into the local hawker centre community.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To further assist these SRHZ users in their transition to the new business environment, NEA will facilitate training for those interested in getting tips on merchandising and display of their items for sale.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA has also put out information on their new business locations so that the SRHZ users' clientele and those who wish to buy second-hand goods can go to these locations after SRHZ closes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Today, the sale of second-hand goods in Singapore is not limited to SRHZ.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nor does it have to be done solely at hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, in some existing flea markets, such as that at Kreta Ayer, which have been in existence for some 15 years, there have always been vendors who sell second-hand goods items.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also recognise that some of the users would prefer not to operate daily and wish to sell their goods at flea markets instead of operating a lock-up stall.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: A majority of those who have chosen to continue their trade at flea markets have, in fact, moved to the Kreta Ayer flea market which is located between Block 4 Sago Lane and Chinatown Complex.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I note that there have also been calls for the Government to engage the users of SRHZ deeply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over the past few months, NEA has been working with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), Workforce Singapore (WSG) and Central Singapore CDC to proactively engage the SRHZ users onsite, as well as offsite, to offer various forms of assistance after the closure of the site.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Besides assistance with getting stalls at hawker centres and flea markets, WSG has been providing job placement assistance to the SRHZ users who wish to seek employment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, one of them is a 61-year-old man who is receiving assistance while he makes the transition to his new job as a cleaner at a primary school.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All in, the agencies have engaged about 200 users of SRHZ, most of whom are between the ages of 40 and 65.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All SRHZ users who are in need of help and have come forward are being assisted.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Another 70 or so had earlier indicated interest to receive assistance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, they have not yet come forward to apply as many of them have indicated that they will decide on their future plans only after the closure of SRHZ.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More than 80 SRHZ users, however, have told us that they do not require any assistance after the closure of SRHZ.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is because they are able to support themselves, or their families can support them, or they have full-time jobs elsewhere.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some have shared that they have been plying their trade at SRHZ as a hobby occasionally on the weekends and will discontinue doing so once SRHZ closes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Besides the assistance given by Government agencies, many Grassroots Advisers and community leaders have also been visiting the SRHZ users residing in their constituencies on a one-on-one basis in their homes to see if they require further community assistance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Those in need have been offered community support, such as job referrals and financial help, to tide them over the transition period.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Others have also been encouraged to join the health and wellness programmes organised by their Residents' Committee (RC) as a good way to stay active after the closure of SRHZ.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We would like to thank all who have given their views and suggestions in support of the SRHZ users.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We would also like to encourage the community to continue to support the SRHZ users, for example, by patronising their stalls in hawker centres and flea markets.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First, how can we help those who have expressed concern that there had been a decline in earnings after moving to hawker centres and flea markets?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is there any further help in their set-up cost or further rebates?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Question two is whether the Government is following up on the SRHZ users who have not come forward for assistance and say they will wait until the SRHZ closes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also working with them to come up with flyers that they can distribute to let their customers know where they are.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, I understand that there is also help, for instance, from Central CDC, from Mayor Denis Phua and her team, in transitional assistance to help them at the flea market and also at the stalls, and various schemes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And I know also, as I have said, that the Hawkers' Association at Chinatown as well as at Golden Mile have actually welcomed the SRHZ users who are going to set up stalls there and even offered them membership into the Hawkers' Association so that they can integrate into the community.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If they require flea market stalls and so on, we will help them to apply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If they require other assistance, for instance, if they decide to change trade to look for a job, we will also work with the agencies to help them with that.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For those who have not given us their contact information, they can come forward to NEA and we will coordinate this on a whole-of-Government basis.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I just want to ask if the Ministry would still consider the relocation plans that the grassroots committee has actually presented.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, they have the "Robinson Petang 2.0", where they have suggested alternative sites, including how to manage the disamenities.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is important to know that what happened here in Sungei Road is that it is a place-making that is very, very genuine and real.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: By removing it, we are actually taking away that place-making possibility.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: If there is something that is already ground-up and alive, why take it away?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Why not have a relocation, put them there and, at the same time, manage the disamenities which I think is something that we can do?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said earlier, we understand that SRHZ holds fond memories for a number of Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, because of that, we have got NHB to do research as well as documentation and put this up together with the virtual tour on their heritage portal.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SRHZ used to be a place where you could find very unique antiques, knick-knacks and so on but, over time, the nature of the site has changed, both in terms of the profile of the users of the site, as well as the buyers and the type of goods sold.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, if you go to SHRZ now, the most common type of goods sold there, are not necessarily second-hand goods, but second-hand goods, such as clothes, watches, handphone covers, cables, as well as shoes, that is, goods that are not unique to or only sold at SRHZ.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, you can find them in neighbourhood shops, too.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, the sale of second-hand goods is not limited to SRHZ.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, by offering them, say, lock-up stalls, it is a more sustainable permanent solution, and they can actually use it to expand their offerings beyond what they are selling currently.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, during transition, there is bound to be some uncertainties, and we are doing our very best to help them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, notwithstanding this, obviously, if there are other ground-up efforts in terms of flea markets that the community wants to create and put up, some of these SRHZ users conceivably can also join them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have to declare that I have residents in the nearby neighbourhood who have objections to the disamenities caused by the zone for many years, but I also have some residents who are the zone users themselves.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It has been said that the users are elderly and dependent on the business at SRHZ for a living.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some also said that it is good for the elderly to be active, to push the carts in the elements and set up stalls elsewhere.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And by giving such priority, are there also objections to these priorities given?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Can other community groups at the grassroots level also be engaged to help resolve these issues?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the first question on how many users rely on SRHZ for their livelihoods, based on our engagement with these users on the ground as well as how the health of the SRHZ users would be affected with the closure of SRHZ, let me say, as I have replied in my response earlier, that we have engaged more than 200 SRHZ users.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Just by way of comparison, during the weekends, which is the peak of SRHZ when most of the users will be there to ply their trade and sell their goods, there are usually about 200 SRHZ users.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They go to SRHZ to ply their goods perhaps on the weekends.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For some, they say they ply their goods as a hobby and they have decided to stop after the closure of SRHZ although, if they wish to, they can actually continue at the flea markets.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have helped all those who have come forward to ask for assistance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More than 60 have been assisted, one way or the other.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Sixteen have been given flea market stalls, and some have already started operating.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They have embraced change and decided to move on and have, in fact, started operating their stalls.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members of the community who are concerned could also help them, for instance, by patronising their stalls.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the other 70, they have actually come forward and said they may need help, but that they want to wait until after the closure of SRHZ to decide and, as I have said earlier, we will help them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to see how we can assist them after the closure.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think that the users of SRHZ do not need to ply their trade in order to stay healthy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, pushing the cart and so on may actually be detrimental to their health if they do not do it properly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have many programmes in the community, for instance, the PA's health and wellness programmes that our seniors can participate in to stay socially active and engaged, and also physically active.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition to that, she also asked how we can make sure that we continue to engage them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, our place managers do visit the SRHZ users who have already set up stalls at the markets and even at the flea markets to see how they are doing, and to see if additional assistance needs to be rendered.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding relocation, I think I have answered that earlier.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun also asked about relocation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, the nature of SRHZ has changed over the years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, we have allowed SRHZ to continue for as long as possible, but now that it is needed for redevelopment and we have to close it, plus the nature of the site has changed over the years and given that the sale of such goods is not just limited to SRHZ, we have helped them to relocate to other areas, like hawker centres as well as flea markets.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I have also noted that there is a natural clustering now.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Most of the SRHZ users are now relocated either in Chinatown Market or in Golden Mile Food Centre, as well as the Kreta Ayer flea market, all of which are actually very near SRHZ and all of which, if you look at it, the goods sold are not really incompatible with what the SRHZ users are selling.
